sources.title: Presidential Decree 189/23: simplified tourist-visa procedure
sources.officialityEvidence: The live Government/CIPRA PDF is Decree 189/23, published in Diário da República I Series no. 185 of 29 September 2023. Article 4(4)-(5) makes the official SME route a lawful tourist-visa channel and specifies frontier affixation after its electronic pre-authorisation.

sources.officialityEvidence: The live central Government page identifies Decree 189/23, confirms its tourist-only scope and current simplified consular and SME tourist-visa procedures, including the maximum decision period.

sources.title: SME eVISA official tourist-visa page
sources.officialityEvidence: The live SME page directly names Taiwan in its country selector but does not list South Sudan or Kosovo. Its selector is not an eligibility schedule: its displayed country options all submit the same generic value, so absence cannot negate Article 4 but it does not independently establish omitted-document operational acceptance.

policies.title: Ordinary passports: Angola pre-authorised tourist visa affixed at frontier
policies.summary: Decree 189/23 Article 4 establishes a broad tourist-visa route: the traveller applies through SME, receives electronic pre-authorisation and presents it at the frontier, where the visa is physically affixed to the travel document. Under the issuance-point taxonomy this is visa_on_arrival, not evisa. The cohort excludes current unverified document-recognition/operational cases and preserved-treaty conflicts.
conditions: Ordinary passport short tourist visits only; not work, study, medical treatment, residence, transit, diplomatic, official/service, emergency or special-document cases.
Apply through the official SME channel before travel, obtain the electronic pre-authorisation, present it at the frontier, and receive the visa affixed in the travel document after confirmation.
Passport validity must exceed six months; round-trip ticket and an international vaccination certificate are required where applicable.
The decision period is no more than three working days. Border admission remains subject to confirmation and other applicable formalities.
An alternative simplified consular tourist-visa procedure exists; it does not change the available online-preauthorisation/frontier-issuance route.
Article 3(3) preserves treaty and agreement commitments. This policy therefore excludes São Tomé and Príncipe and Zambia while their bilateral ordinary-passport baseline remains unresolved.

application.label: Serviço de Migração e Estrangeiros tourist-visa pre-authorisation
application.processingTime: Decree 189/23 Article 4 provides a decision within no more than three working days.
steps: Submit the tourist-visa request through the official SME channel before travel.
Receive the electronic entry pre-authorisation through that channel.
Present it and the required valid ordinary passport, return ticket and any applicable vaccination certificate at the frontier for confirmation and visa affixation.

unresolved.reason: Article 4 is generally framed, but the current SME country selector omits South Sudan while naming Sudan. The portal is not a schedule, so omission cannot prove ineligibility; however it supplies no reproducible current operational mapping for a South Sudan ordinary passport to the required online pre-authorisation/frontier route. The conservative cohort holds SS pending such a mapping.

The current SME selector omits Kosovo and no current Angolan primary source directly establishes acceptance/recognition of an ordinary Kosovo passport for the Article 4 online pre-authorisation and frontier-affixation procedure. Generic statutory wording cannot safely supply that document-specific operational fact.

Article 3(3) preserves international agreements. Angola's current Government register describes São Tomé and Príncipe only as a tourist-visa-facilitation partner; it does not establish whether a bilateral ordinary-passport rule displaces or conditions the Article 4 default. Hold rather than overwrite the imported visa-free baseline.

Article 3(3) preserves international agreements. Zambia Immigration describes a current ordinary-passport no-visa bilateral rule, but Angola's Government register later calls the arrangement tourist-visa facilitation. The conflict blocks both visa-free and Article 4 visa_on_arrival normalization.
